# DeskVNC, full reference

> DeskVNC is a native desktop client for VNC, RDP and SSH, written in Rust on Tauri 2, running on Windows, macOS and Linux, dual licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0. It ships an MCP server named dvv that lets an AI agent drive a real remote desktop over the protocol the machine already speaks, with nothing installed on the remote machine and with a person able to take control back at any moment. Repository: https://github.com/psmux/DeskVNC

## The observe-then-act loop

An agent drives a desktop by looping: `dvv_hosts` lists what there is to open, `dvv_open` with `perceive: true` returns a limbId, a size and a state, `dvv_control` with `action: "acquire"` takes the lease, `dvv_screen` reads the picture and prints an `imageSpace` line plus a `generation`, `dvv_click` acts while carrying that generation, `dvv_screen` with `form: "damage-crop"` looks again at only the region that changed, then `dvv_type` and `dvv_key` continue.

```jsonc
dvv_hosts   {}
dvv_open    {"hostId": "<id>", "perceive": true}
dvv_control {"limbId": "...", "action": "acquire"}
dvv_screen  {"limbId": "...", "form": "full", "scale": 0.25}
dvv_click   {"limbId": "...", "x": 700, "y": 400, "generation": 1}
```

Measured on a real 1920x1080 Windows desktop over LAN, one full observe-then-act cycle takes 19 ms, about 52 actions per second. dvv_open and attach take 4 ms, dvv_control acquire is under 1 ms, dvv_screen at scale 0.25 takes 25 ms, and dvv_type runs at 447 characters per second.

## The generation fence

A click computed against a screen that has since changed is refused rather than landing in the wrong place, and typing and key presses are refused until the screen has been read since it last changed significantly. With scale 0.5, a point at (mx, my) on the picture is (mx*2, my*2) on the machine. Handle LIMB_GONE by listing limbs and reopening the machine, and SCREEN_CHANGED by reading the screen again and retrying.

## Human take-back

The person at the remote machine can take control back at any moment, and can revoke control or end the session. In an attended Boundary support session they approve the connection first, no account is required, and Boundary tries a direct encrypted path before falling back to a relay.

## Machines that refuse installed agents

Funded tools that let an agent use a Windows desktop all install an agent on that desktop, which is refused on Citrix, on VDI, on jump hosts and on anything a client owns. DeskVNC speaks VNC, RDP or SSH, the protocols those machines already answer on, so the connection the environment already permits is the one the agent travels over.
